courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So we're nearing the end,
what's missing is that we can book a place. Right now if we book, we get this action bar and here in
this modal, I want to render a nice form that allows a user to enter some booking details, like let's
say a first name, a last name, the number of guests that will stay here,
I mean I'll name this app pairbnb
but maybe you want to bring an extra guest for more fun or whatever.
So let's say you can pick more than two people, let's say you can pick if you're coming alone because you're
a pretty sad pair or you're coming with your partner or you're coming with your partner and a good friend.
So I wanna have a dropdown that allows us to pick the number of guests and I'll also of course want to render
some date inputs here where we can pick the range in which we want to stay at this place.
So that will be the form that I want to build here and I will build it entirely with the template-driven
approach.
Let's go back to code and let's have a look at the modal here,
that is our create booking page here of course where we have that book button right now and only the place
description up here.
I don't care so much about the description,
instead now it's about rendering a nice form. For that form here on the create booking page or this component,
let's add an ion-grid
so that we have full control over the positioning and an ion-column where I will add a size-sm
of six and offset-sm of three for nice centering and less width on bigger devices and in the first
column here, I want to fetch the first name of a person.
So I'll add an ion-item here with an ion-label where I say first name and the position of this label will be
floating. Below that we have the ion-input with type of text and then since I will use the template-driven
approach, ngModel added, a name added which here can be first-name for example and I'll
also add the required validator.
Now I can also already wrap the entire grid with a form here because as I mentioned, I will use the template
driven approach and therefore we'll need that form tag for Angular to detect this. By the way, for that
it's always important that the module that declares create booking imports the forms module.
Now back to this template here.
This is the first row I want to add with the first name,
now it's not the only one, I'll duplicate that to also get the last name here, the name here on the input
can be last name therefore, type is still text of course
and then I want to have the number of guests.
So let's render another
row here and the label could say number of guests
and then here, I'll not use an ion-input but another component which we haven't seen yet, an ion-select.
Now you probably know the default HTML select, which is the default HTML dropdown and ion-select works
pretty much the same.
It is a wrapper around the default HTML select element you could say and as always, the official
Ionic docs are the place to go to learn all about this component.
So ion-select now gets a name which is guest number
and also receives ngModel here.
However here, I will bind ngModel with square brackets to a default value of two and this is important
because I'll now add three options and I want to preselect option 2,
we can change that but I want to start with that one selected so that there is always a selection for
this.
So let's now add an ion-select-option and such an option needs a value and for me, the values will be 1, 2
and 3.
So here, I'll start with value 1 and then what actually gets displayed on the screen is entered between
the opening closing tag of ion-select-option,
so here it's 1.
Now I'll also have 2 and 3 and also update the value here which is the data that is received behind
the scenes
and we're good and now because I have value 2 here and I set the entire select to a default value
of 2, this option here will be preselected. Now let's have a look at the dates because there, we'll do more
than we did before.
